message.content:
Design a detailed implementation plan for redesigning TaptPay's customer-facing checkout pages at /home/runner/workspace (React+TS client in client/src, wouter routing, Express server in server/, Drizzle schema in shared/schema.ts). Verify file/line claims below by reading the key files before finalizing.

# The redesign (user-supplied mockups in attached_assets/, 2026-07-11)

All pages become: off-white page bg, centered rounded navy card (#040D6D), "taptpay" wordmark (serif, "tapt" bold + "pay" italic — the Larken font used on the landing page, see client/public/assets/ fonts), sky-blue (#58ABFF) text, huge amount figure, minimal chrome. Brand tokens already exist in client/src/lib/trades-theme.ts (INK #040D6D, ACCENT #58ABFF, OFFW #F4F4F4).

Per-vertical content:
- Retail/hospo: label ("lunch"), amount, dark Google Pay pill (existing branded asset), footer link "enter credit card ∨" expanding a card-entry panel that is now SKY BLUE (#58ABFF) instead of dark.
- Property: address as title, amount, subtitle e.g. "weekly rent payment", same pay controls.
- Trades WITH deposit — a single page that animates through 3 steps:
  1. Title (job/quote description), FULL quote amount, subtitle "10% deposit required", one outline button "view quote" → opens existing quote PDF (/api/trades/quotes/token/:token/pdf).
  2. After the quote has been viewed/closed, the button animates: "confirm" outline button slides over with a small square QR-style icon button beside it that re-opens the quote PDF.
  3. On confirm, quote is accepted server-side and the card animates to the standard payment layout: deposit amount large ($250), subtitle "10% deposit of $2,500", GPay + "enter credit card ∨".
- Trades WITHOUT deposit: just the standard payment page (step 3 layout, full amount).
- Split payment (retail /split/:transactionId): chip "Person 1 of 2", label, amount, − N + person stepper, "enter amount" custom-amount input, confirm button — same behavior as today (2–10 people, equal shares, custom amount validated against total, SSE live updates, subsequent payers see remaining), just restyled.

User decisions: restyle applies to ALL verticals' checkout; split behavior unchanged (restyle only); merchant customLogoUrl support must be kept (custom logo replaces wordmark); QR icon button = re-open quote PDF; "view quote" = existing PDF.

# Current code map (from a completed exploration — verify before relying)

- Routes in client/src/App.tsx:356–373: /r/:token and /checkout/:transactionId → pages/checkout.tsx; /split/:transactionId → pages/split-payment.tsx; /pay/:merchantId → customer-payment.tsx (redirect page, not UI); /trades/quote/:token → pages/trades/quote-response.tsx (Accept/Decline page — the new 3-step flow replaces its customer-facing role).
- client/src/pages/checkout.tsx (1659 lines): the single HPP for retail transactions AND property/trades invoices. isInvoice = !!token (line ~74). Uses plain inline CSSProperties style constants at ~1466–1651 matching hpp-preview.html (page bg #f0f4ff, blue card #0055FF radius 48, cyan #00E5CC accents). Payment wiring that MUST be preserved untouched: Apple Pay pre-session + native button (~239–298, ~704–711, ~823), Google Pay (~302–326, ~940, button ~1300), Windcave Hosted Fields lazy-load + #hf-* mounts (~329–342, ~658, ~1373–1405), the Windcave HPP navigation-guard block (~349–601), endpoints switch (~87–89), /api/windcave/env (~204), IS_MOCK short-circuit (~81–84). Inline invoice split UI at ~1153–1202 (restyle to match, behavior unchanged). Merchant logo + teal CSS filter ~1025–1036.
- Invoice resolve: GET /api/checkout/resolve/:token (server/routes.ts:~6058) unions property invoices_rent_requests + trades job_invoices, returns vertical ("property"|"trades"), kind (rent/charge | deposit/balance/full/recurring), description, documentUrl, split fields. No quote data today.
- Trades quotes: shared/schema.ts ~989–1020 (quotes: lineItems, depositEnabled, depositType percent|fixed, depositValue, depositCents, token, status). Quote respond endpoint near server/routes.ts:6791: POST /api/trades/quotes/token/:token/respond — on accept creates kind:"deposit" (or "full") job_invoice and returns paymentUrl (an /r/:token link). Quote PDF: GET /api/trades/quotes/token/:token/pdf.
- split-payment.tsx (457 lines, Tailwind, #0055FF/#00E5CC hexes): first-person state with ± person count 2–10, equal share, custom amount editMode, progress bars, "pay full amount instead"; subsequent-payer state "Person N of M"; SSE transaction_updated + 3s poll; pays via /api/transactions/:id/split then /pay.

# Key design questions for you to resolve in the plan

1. **Trades 3-step entry point**: the user wants ONE page animating through steps. Recommend how: e.g. route /trades/quote/:token to the checkout component in "quote mode" (new resolve or reuse of existing quote fetch used by quote-response.tsx), confirm calls the respond endpoint, then the page swaps its token to the returned deposit-invoice token and continues to the payment step WITHOUT a hard navigation (or with one — weigh it). Consider: Apple Pay/GPay pre-sessions are created on load for a known amount/token — check whether they're created per-invoice and whether swapping token mid-page breaks them; a clean option is animating steps 1–2 then doing location.href to the /r/:token payment page, but weigh UX (user explicitly wants it to feel like one animated page). Check what quote-response.tsx fetches (GET endpoint for quote by token) for reuse. Also handle: quote already accepted (link revisited) → jump straight to step 3; declined/expired quotes; keep or drop the Decline action (recommend keeping a subtle text link; note it).
2. **Where the new styling lives**: recommend a shared style/token module (e.g. extend or parallel trades-theme, or a new checkout-theme.ts) + whether to keep inline-style approach of checkout.tsx or convert to Tailwind (checkout.tsx is inline styles; split-payment.tsx is Tailwind — minimal-risk recommendation preferred; a restyle should not rewrite payment logic).
3. **Wordmark**: text-based "taptpay" using the Larken font (check client/public/assets and landing.css for @font-face names) vs image asset; must still swap for customLogoUrl.
4. **Sky-blue card-entry panel**: the expanded hosted-fields panel becomes #58ABFF background — note hosted-fields iframe styling implications (Windcave hosted fields take style config? check how current styles are passed, ~658 controller creation) and contrast (navy text on sky blue).
5. **Animation approach** for step transitions (framer-motion is likely already a dep — check package.json; landing uses motion; keep it light).
6. What happens to quote-response.tsx (it may still serve email-link recipients — check who links to /trades/quote/:token: server/trades-delivery.ts etc.) — recommend redirect or removal.
7. Property subtitle ("weekly rent payment") — derive from invoice kind/frequency fields (check invoices_rent_requests schema for frequency) with sensible fallback.
8. Sequencing into safe, verifiable stages + a verification section (dev server, VITE_MOCK=1 mock mode exists in checkout.tsx — use it; headless screenshots per vertical; how to fabricate test tokens for property/trades/quote flows — check for seed scripts or dev routes).

Deliver: a step-by-step implementation plan with concrete file paths, functions/endpoints to reuse, new components/modules to create, per-stage acceptance checks, and explicit "do not touch" list for the payment wiring. Flag any risks you find while verifying (e.g. pre-session/token coupling, GPay button asset colors, iOS webview quirks referenced in the code).

- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

export const quotes = pgTable("quotes", {
  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
  merchantId: integer("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id).notNull(),
  clientProfileId: uuid("client_profile_id").references(() => clientProfiles.id).notNull(),
  token: text("token").notNull().unique(),
  // draft · sent · viewed · accepted · declined · expired

  lineItems: jsonb("line_items").notNull(),

  gstCents: integer("gst_cents").notNull().default(0),
  gstMode: text("gst_mode"),
  totalCents: integer("total_cents").notNull(),
  depositEnabled: boolean("deposit_enabled").notNull().default(false),
  depositType: text("deposit_type"),        // 'percent' | 'fixed'
  depositValue: integer("deposit_value"),    // percent (0-100) or cents
  depositCents: integer("deposit_cents"),    // computed deposit amount in cents
  deliveryChannel: text("delivery_channel").notNull().default("email"),
  validUntil: timestamp("valid_until"),
  notes: text("notes"),
  documentUrl: text("document_url"),
  documentName: text("document_name"),
  sentAt: timestamp("sent_at"),
  viewedAt: timestamp("viewed_at"),
  acceptedAt: timestamp("accepted_at"),
  declinedAt: timestamp("declined_at"),

}, (t) => ({

  tokenIdx: index("quotes_token_idx").on(t.token),
}));

export const jobSchedules = pgTable("job_schedules", {
  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
  merchantId: integer("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id).notNull(),
  clientProfileId: uuid("client_profile_id").references(() => clientProfiles.id).notNull(),
  amountCents: integer("amount_cents").notNull(),

  startDate: timestamp("start_date").notNull(),
  endDate: timestamp("end_date"),
  nextRunDate: timestamp("next_run_date").notNull(),
  lastRunDate: timestamp("last_run_date"),
  status: text("status").notNull().default("active"),

export const jobInvoices = pgTable("job_invoices", {
  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
  merchantId: integer("merchant_id").references(() => merchants.id).notNull(),
  clientProfileId: uuid("client_profile_id").references(() => clientProfiles.id).notNull(),

  kind: text("kind").notNull().default("full"),
  amountCents: integer("amount_cents").notNull(),
  token: text("token").notNull().unique(),
  deliveryChannel: text("delivery_channel").notNull(),
  jobDetails: text("job_details"),
  status: text("status").notNull().default("pending_dispatch"),
  dueAt: timestamp("due_at").notNull(),
  dispatchedAt: timestamp("dispatched_at"),
  sentAt: timestamp("sent_at"),
  viewedAt: timestamp("viewed_at"),
  paidAt: timestamp("paid_at"),
  voidedAt: timestamp("voided_at"),
  completedAt: timestamp("completed_at"),
  externalPaymentReference: text("external_payment_reference"),
  lastReminderSentAt: timestamp("last_reminder_sent_at"),
  scheduledSendAt: timestamp("scheduled_send_at"),
  reminderCount: integer("reminder_count").notNull().default(0),
  documentUrl: text("document_url"),
  documentName: text("document_name"),
  windcaveSessionId: text("windcave_session_id"),
  windcaveTransactionId: text("windcave_transaction_id"),
  splitEnabled: boolean("split_enabled").notNull().default(false),
  splitCount: integer("split_count"),
  splitPaidCount: integer("split_paid_count").notNull().default(0),
  splitPaidSessions: text("split_paid_sessions").array(),
  splitPayerEmails: text("split_payer_emails").array(),
  whatsappMessageId: text("whatsapp_message_id"),
  whatsappDeliveredAt: timestamp("whatsapp_delivered_at"),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at").defaultNow(),
}, (t) => ({
  statusDueIdx: index("job_invoices_status_due_idx").on(t.status, t.dueAt),
  merchantStatusIdx: index("job_invoices_merchant_status_idx").on(t.merchantId, t.status),
  tokenIdx: index("job_invoices_token_idx").on(t.token),
  // One LIVE recurring invoice per (schedule, due date) — makes cron generation
  // idempotent under concurrent/retried runs. Partial so non-recurring invoices
  // (null scheduleId) never collide, and voided rows are excluded so a cancelled
  // duplicate can't wedge the index.
  scheduleDueUq: uniqueIndex("job_invoices_schedule_due_uq").on(t.scheduleId, t.dueAt).where(sql`${t.scheduleId} IS NOT NULL AND ${t.status} <> 'voided'`),
}));

Use it; don't add the parallel `motion@12` import to these pages. - Mock mode confirmed: `client/src/mocks/mock-api.ts` covers `/api/transactions/:id` (DEMO_TX id 90210), `/api/checkout/resolve/:token` (unknown token → payable rent fallback; `job_` tokens → trades), `/api/merchants/:id`, `/api/windcave/env`. In quote mode there is no invoice token until confirm, so `payId` is null, `transaction` is null, and **no session is ever created for a stale amount**. Trades 3-step entry point** — Keep `/trades/quote/:token` as the customer URL (it's baked into sent emails/SMS via `server/trades-delivery.ts:74` and into the quote PDF's accept link via `server/trades-quote-pdf.ts:163`). Inside checkout.tsx: - `const quoteToken = quoteMode ? params.token : undefined;` `const [acceptedInvoiceToken, setAcceptedInvoiceToken] = useState(null);` `const token = quoteMode ? acceptedInvoiceToken ?? undefined : params.token;` — everything downstream (`isInvoice`, `payId`, endpoints) flows from `token` unchanged. - New `useQuery` on `GET /api/trades/quotes/token/:token` (enabled in quote mode only; same fetch quote-response.tsx uses today). - Step 1: title = first line item description, amount = `quote.totalCents`, subtitle = `"${depositValue}% deposit required"` (or "deposit required" for fixed type; no deposit → "quote total"), one outline "view quote" button → `window.open('/api/trades/quotes/token/${quoteToken}/pdf', '_blank')`. - Step 2: after the PDF has been opened (track `quoteViewed` state set on click; also start at step 2 if `quote.viewedAt` is already set), animate the button row: "confirm" outline button + square QR-style icon button that re-opens the same PDF. - Confirm: `POST /api/trades/quotes/token/:token/respond {accept:true}` → take `depositInvoice.token` from the response → `setAcceptedInvoiceToken(token)` and `history.replaceState(null, "", "/r/" + token)` (so refresh/share lands on the payment page; the nav guard only blocks Windcave URLs, so this is safe). The card content crossfades to the standard payment layout — **no navigation, one animated page**, and the wallet pre-sessions initialize fresh at that moment (verified safe above). - Revisited accepted link → jump straight to step 3 using the server extension below. Declined → "quote declined" state; expired (410/status) → "quote expired" state. **Keep Decline** as a subtle underlined text link under the confirm row (endpoint already supports it and notifies the merchant); note this to the user since the mockups omit it. - Rejected alternative: `location.href` to `/r/:token` after confirm — simpler but a full reload mid-animation; the user explicitly wants one animated page, and the in-place swap is verified safe. **Server extension (small, additive):** in `GET /api/trades/quotes/token/:token` (routes.ts:6738), when `quote.status === "accepted"`, look up the latest non-voided `job_invoice` with `quoteId = quote.id` and `kind in ('deposit','full')` and include `invoice: { token, kind, amountCents, status } | null` in the response. Add the two `@font-face` rules (copied from landing.css:7–8) to a new `client/src/styles/checkout.css` imported by the three checkout pages (duplicating the face declarations is harmless — same src, browser dedupes via cache). Sky-blue card-entry panel** — The expander becomes a plain footer text link "enter credit card ∨" at the bottom of the navy card (replacing the cyan tab); the expanding panel (currently `#00E5CC`, checkout.tsx:1354–1364) becomes `#58ABFF`. Update `hfContainerStyle`, `formLabelStyle` (navy labels — navy on #58ABFF is ~4.5:1, acceptable for the 11px bold uppercase labels but prefer near-white `#0B1230`→ use INK and bump weight), pay button (INK bg, white text), and `threeDsIFrame.overlayBgColor` from `{r:0,g:85,b:255}` to `{r:4,g:13,b:109}`. **Critical constraint:** the panel container and `#hf-number/#hf-expiry/#hf-cvv/#hf-name` mounts must stay always-rendered with `maxHeight: 0` when collapsed, exactly as today (1354–1423) — do not conditionally unmount them. **5.
